items.front: Original size of the Constitution (1949)?
items.back: 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules (now about 470/25/12).
items.examPoint: Lengthiest written constitution — original vs current count
items.source: notes

items.front: Which article calls India a 'Union of States'?
items.back: Article 1 — implies no right to secede; word 'Federation' is never used.
items.source: notes

items.front: Borrowed: Fundamental Rights & judicial review from?
items.back: United States (also VP's post, independence of judiciary).
items.source: notes

items.front: Borrowed: DPSP and Fundamental Duties from?
items.back: DPSP — Ireland; Fundamental Duties — USSR (Soviet).
items.examPoint: Sources borrowed — Irish DPSP, Soviet FD
items.source: notes

items.front: The Preamble is based on which document?
items.back: The Objectives Resolution, moved by Jawaharlal Nehru (1946).
items.source: notes

items.front: Which words did the 42nd Amendment (1976) add to the Preamble?
items.back: Socialist, Secular and Integrity.
items.source: notes

items.front: Five keywords describing the state in the Preamble?
items.back: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.
items.source: notes

items.front: Four objectives in the Preamble?
items.back: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
items.source: notes

items.front: Berubari (1960) vs Kesavananda (1973) on the Preamble?
items.back: Berubari: NOT part of the Constitution; Kesavananda: IS part and is amendable.
items.source: notes

items.front: Is the Preamble enforceable in court?
items.back: No — it is non-justiciable (LIC 1995: integral part but not directly enforceable).
items.source: notes

items.front: Adoption and commencement dates of the Constitution?
items.back: Adopted 26 Nov 1949; came into force 26 Jan 1950.
items.source: notes

items.front: Which Schedule lists official languages and how many?
items.back: 8th Schedule — 22 languages.
items.source: notes

items.front: 9th and 10th Schedules cover what (and via which amendments)?
items.back: 9th: land-reform laws (1st Amdt 1951); 10th: Anti-Defection (52nd Amdt 1985).
items.source: notes

items.front: Parts: III, IV and IVA cover what?
items.back: III = Fundamental Rights; IV = DPSP; IVA = Fundamental Duties (51A).
items.source: notes

items.front: In which languages was the original Constitution handwritten?
items.back: In both Hindi and English.
items.examPoint: All 25 Parts with Article ranges and all 12 Schedules with their Articles; Article 371D/371E (Andhra Pradesh)

items.front: Why does the Constitution put details in Schedules?
items.back: To keep detailed lists out of the main text and make amending them easier.
items.examPoint: All 25 Parts with Article ranges and all 12 Schedules with their Articles; Article 371D/371E (Andhra Pradesh)

items.front: True or false: "Republic" in the Preamble means an elected head of State, the PM.
items.back: False. It means an elected President, not the PM.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Preamble was enacted before the rest of the Constitution.
items.back: False. It was enacted last, so it fits the whole text.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Preamble is part of the Constitution but not enforceable in court.
items.back: True. Kesavananda (1973) made it a part; courts use it only to interpret.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Union Territories are in the "Territory of India" but not the "Union of India".
items.back: True. The Union of India means the states only.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The phrase "Territory of India" is not found in the Constitution.
items.back: False. Both phrases are in Art 1.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Art 31B stopped working after the I.R. Coelho case (2007).
items.back: False. It still works. Coelho opened only post-24 April 1973 entries to review.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Ninth Schedule entries are limited to land reform laws.
items.back: False. They go beyond land reform, e.g. Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation law.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The office of Governor is a federal feature.
items.back: False. A Centre-appointed Governor is a unitary feature.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: Indian secularism protects non-believers too.
items.back: True. Freedom of religion is for every person, believer or not.
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: True or false: The Law Commission circulated a UCC questionnaire in October 2016.
items.back: True. The 21st Law Commission (Justice B. S. Chauhan).
items.source: APPSC Group-I/II previous papers with official keys

items.front: Citizenship — which Part and Articles?
items.back: Part II, Articles 5-11. Article 11 lets Parliament regulate citizenship by law (Citizenship Act, 1955).
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: Five ways to acquire Indian citizenship (Act of 1955)?
items.back: Birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: Three ways to lose Indian citizenship?
items.back: Renunciation (by choice), termination (automatic on taking another citizenship), deprivation (Central Government order).
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: CAA 2019 — who, from where, cut-off?
items.back: Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan; entry by 31 Dec 2014; naturalised after 5 years.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: Is OCI dual citizenship?
items.back: No. OCI (2005) is a life-long visa for foreign citizens of Indian origin; no vote, no constitutional office. PIO merged into it in 2015.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: Citizenship by birth for someone born after 3 December 2004?
items.back: Both parents citizens, or one citizen and the other not an illegal migrant.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: Article 343 — official language of the Union?
items.back: Hindi in Devanagari, with the international form of numerals; English for 15 years. The 1963 Act keeps English with no end date.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan

items.front: Kasturi Lal (1965) held what?
items.back: The state is not liable for wrongs done in a sovereign function (police custody). N. Nagendra Rao (1997) narrowed this rule.
items.source: Constitution of India (Parts II, XIV, XVI, XVII); Citizenship Act 1955; standard polity text (Laxmikanth) chapter plan
